exercises.title: A growable array
exercises.task: Vec is a growable array built the way Go's append works underneath: a fixed array, and a bigger copy when it is full. Press Run: it shows each time the array grows, the total number of copies for a million pushes, and how Go's own slices grow.

exercises.title: Write Push
exercises.task: Fill the two holes in Push: choose the new capacity (double it), then allocate the bigger array and copy the elements. Check also counts the copies: doubling keeps them under 2 per element.
hints: Growing by one each time works, but copies everything on every push: n²/2 copies in total. Doubling makes growing rare.
When len(v.data) is 0, doubling gives 0: start at 1.
Hole 2: bigger := make([]int, newCap), a loop that copies v.data[i] into bigger[i] for i below v.n (count each one), then v.data = bigger.

exercises.title: Two commands, one array
exercises.task: WithFlag builds a command line from a base list of arguments and one extra flag. Run it: the two commands it builds end up with the same flag. Fix WithFlag so each result has its own array.
hints: base has spare capacity. append writes into it in place, so both calls write to the same slot of the same array.
Give the result its own array: make a slice with room for one more element, then copy base into it.
out := make([]string, len(base), len(base)+1), copy(out, base), return append(out, flag).
